Title: BN ready to include PN in Melaka government if coalition wins
Article:
TANGGA BATU: Barisan Nasional (BN) is ready to bring Perikatan Nasional (PN) into the Melaka government if the two coalitions win the state election.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said cooperation between the two coalitions should continue beyond the election, including through the formation of a joint state government.
"After Nov 14, as BN chairman, if BN and PN are blessed with victory, God willing, the Melaka government will also involve PN in its formation.
"Let us put aside our past differences. We should not stop at Melaka because we have a much bigger task ahead of us.
"God willing, if we secure a strong majority in the state legislative assembly, particularly in the seats we are contesting, it will demonstrate that BN and PN can reach a consensus and move forward together towards building a new political home at the national level," he said.
He was speaking at the BN-PN grand finale campaign event for the Paya Rumput state constituency here tonight.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the cooperation reflected the willingness of both coalitions to set aside their past political differences in pursuit of greater unity among Muslims.
He described Melaka as a starting point for closer political cooperation between the two coalitions, which could eventually be extended to the national level.
"This bigger home is one that we are building for the entire ummah. It is a home that brings together our shared aspirations without sidelining other religions, races, cultures or languages.
"Pas has demonstrated through its policies that it is capable of reaching out to people of different religions and ethnic backgrounds."

Title: Subsidy leakages: RM82.85mil worth of goods seized in 5,893 cases since 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 5,893 cases involving the abuse and leakage of controlled and subsidised goods, including cooking oil, diesel and petrol, were recorded nationwide, with seizures worth RM82.85 million, between Jan 1, 2023 and Oct 31 this year.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said diesel accounted for 2,763 cases, involving seizures worth RM59.67 million.
Another 1,722 cases involved petrol, with seizures valued at RM5.43 million, while 1,408 cases involved packet cooking oil, with seizures worth RM17.74 million.
"For diesel, Sarawak recorded the highest number of cases at 623, with seizures valued at RM22,398,348, followed by Sabah with 363 cases involving RM7,653,887 worth of seizures and Kedah with 308 cases involving RM3,776,130.
"For petrol, Kelantan recorded the highest number of cases at 786, with seizures valued at RM351,872.24, followed by Sabah with 629 cases involving RM2,050,806.80 worth of seizures and Perlis with 130 cases involving RM96,263.86.
"For packet cooking oil, Sabah recorded the highest number of cases at 254, with seizures valued at RM631,494.81, followed by Kelantan with 220 cases involving RM877,883.60 worth of goods seized, while Perak ranked third with 137 cases involving RM204,355.46 worth of seizures," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website tonight.
He was responding to Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu), who sought statistics on cases involving the abuse and leakage of subsidised diesel, petrol and packet cooking oil from 2023 to date, broken down by state, as well as the number of arrests and punishments imposed.
Armizan said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) would continue to intensify enforcement through intelligence-led operations, data utilisation, closer monitoring and strategic cooperation between agencies.
He said the High-Level Inter-Agency Coordination Committee on Enforcement to Combat Leakage and Smuggling (JTPAP), chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, had also been activated on March 11.
"Among the strategies implemented is strengthening Ops Tiris, which began in 2023, through Ops Tiris 4.0 (Integrated), by enhancing cooperation among enforcement bodies and relevant government agencies, effective March 16," he said.

Title: Spain hit by nationwide strike over housing crisis ahead of Nov 29 election
Article:
MADRID: Thousands of Spaniards left their workplaces and hit the streets on Wednesday as a general strike sought to crank up pressure on the key issue of housing weeks before a snap election.
Unions reported a "massive" uptake in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, which also aims to up the ante on wages and public services, but business leaders played down the participation.
In Madrid, where many shops opened as normal, demonstrators rallied in the touristic centre and blocked some roads in pickets that were replicated across the country.
Jaime Vazquez, a 48-year-old technician who repairs industrial machinery, told AFP in the Spanish capital that he had downed tools "to ask for a decent home and the regulation of rent prices" as housing costs spiral.
"The future is not very bright, that's why we have to fight to change it, so that my children and my grandchildren are able to access a home," he said.
In Barcelona, school lunch monitor Ines Oliveras said she wanted "to live a normal life, have my own space, my own home, not have to count every euro just to be able to buy food."
"It's not just my problem, but a shared one... it's very intergenerational," the 29-year-old told AFP.
The size of later demonstrations planned in Madrid and Barcelona will be seen as an indicator of public discontent before the Nov 29 vote, which the right-wing opposition is predicted to win.
- TRAINS DISRUPTED -
The impact on industry and services in the European Union's fourth-largest economy will also be scrutinised, as public transport suffered disruption even with the implementation of minimum service requirements.
In Barcelona, the metro and bus networks were out of action after offering minimum services during the morning rush hour, but Madrid's suburban trains reported little impact on services.
Public rail operator Renfe said 24 per cent of its high-speed services were cancelled, while around 20 per cent of trains were scrapped in the sprawling commuter networks of Madrid and Barcelona.
UGT union leader Pepe Alvarez told public broadcaster RTVE that the participation was "massive", with a "total" stoppage in some regions making the strike "a huge success."
But his union acknowledged participation was "uneven", with large mobilisation in the car manufacturing, petrochemicals and meat sectors and in coastal regions.
The CEOE organisation, which represents business leaders, said in a statement that the impact varied by region and area of work, with a "low participation" in most sectors.
Electricity demand had fallen by around five percent, "significantly lower" than in previous strikes, the CEOE said.
- 'LISTEN TO EVERYONE' -
The main UGT and CCOO unions called the strike following a wave of nationwide protests over access to housing, sparked by the eviction in September of an 87-year-old Madrid pensioner.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the election, initially scheduled for 2027, after his minority government failed to secure parliamentary approval for a package of housing measures proposed in response to the demonstrations.
Business groups and the right have rejected the strike, seeing an election-related gambit instead of a genuine labour dispute.
But the unions have insisted the strike is directed against all levels of the state and not only the right, which voted down the government's housing decrees.
They have defended the walkout as an exceptional measure intended to generate broad social pressure for action on soaring housing costs.
Living costs are another major concern, with inflation hitting 4.9 per cent in September and October – its highest level in more than three years.
Isabel Iglesias, a nurse who lives in Madrid, said housing was the issue "that is affecting me the most." She pays a rent of 1,000 euros (US$1,100) with her partner but earns just 1,700 euros a month.
Iglesias, 27, said Sanchez, who has been in power since 2018, "could have done much more" on housing, urging the next government "to listen to everyone and get their act together."--AFP

Title: Gunmen ambush police convoy in Pakistan, killing eight officers
Article:
PESHAWAR: Gunmen attacked a police convoy on its way to an illegal gold mining operation in Pakistan's northwestern region on Wednesday, killing eight officers, officials said.
A senior administrative official in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province's Kohat district told AFP eight police personnel were killed and 13 others were injured.
Militants set two police vehicles on fire during the assault, while two other police vehicles and one private vehicle were missing, the official said.
He said the officers were travelling to an illegal gold mining operation near Gumbat.
A security official in Peshawar confirmed the toll of eight officers killed.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the shooting in the border province where security forces are battling an intensifying militancy they say emanates from Afghanistan – an accusation its Taliban government denies.
A spokesman for a local emergency service earlier on Wednesday said there had been a "firing incident involving police personnel" in Kohat district, adding that rescue workers were treating a dozen wounded officers.
Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been fraught since the Taliban authorities took power in 2021, and worsened after deadly border clashes in October last year that led to near-total closure of the border.
Clashes subsided after mediation, but the conflict intensified again in February, with Pakistan declaring "an open war" on its neighbour.
Islamabad accuses Kabul of allowing militants responsible for deadly attacks on Pakistani territory to operate from its soil. Afghanistan's Taliban authorities have denied the allegations.
Hundreds of civilians have been killed in fighting between the two countries since October last year, according to figures from the United Nations' mission in Afghanistan.
Earlier this month, militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa killed two police officers assigned to protect a polio vaccination team travelling near the Afghan border.
The province was placed under emergency rule last month in a move authorities said came in reaction to the failure by the provincial government to act against militancy.
The imposition of emergency measures sidelined the last remaining bastion of power for jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
The special constitutional measures also set off a province-wide crackdown on Khan's supporters, with hundreds of detentions.--AFP

Title: Spain investigates alleged child sexual abuse material on TikTok
Article:
MADRID: Spanish prosecutors on Wednesday ordered an investigation into the alleged distribution of child sexual abuse material on TikTok, following a complaint filed by anti-disinformation group Maldita.es.
A prosecutor has been appointed to investigate possible offences involving the production and distribution of child sexual abuse material and the corruption of minors on the social media platform, Spain's public prosecutor's office said in a statement.
It follows a complaint submitted to the office's cybercrime unit by Maldita.es, which on Monday accused TikTok of not doing enough to prevent paedophiles from accessing child sexual abuse material or soliciting images from children on the platform.
"Material you would expect to find only on the dark web is on TikTok," the Maldita.es association said.
In the investigation published Monday, Maldita.es catalogued more than 1,000 videos of child abuse footage, which had been viewed a total of 48 million times.
Maldita.es further alleged that TikTok had removed only a tenth of the material it flagged and blocked just 26 per cent of illegal posts in Spain.
The complaint to prosecutors cites the publication, distribution and sale of child abuse material on the platform, as well as users directing others to similar content on TikTok and other platforms.
It also raises concerns about live broadcasts featuring minors in exchange for financial compensation.
Representatives of Maldita.es appeared before a prosecutor on Wednesday to formally confirm their complaint and submit supporting evidence, the public prosecutor's office said.
TikTok, owned by Chinese parent company ByteDance, faces a wave of lawsuits and investigations over accusations that it has failed to protect minors, which the company has frequently denied.
On Friday, the EU told TikTok to change the "harmful" design of its personalised For You feed or risk large fines under the bloc's digital content rules.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced a series of measures in February aimed at tackling the "manipulation and amplification of illegal content" on social media, including plans to ban under-16s from accessing the platforms.
The Socialist leader has repeatedly accused X, Meta and TikTok of failing to do enough to tackle the creation and distribution of fake sexual images of minors on their platforms.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 150 Bersatu members quit party ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 150 members of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) in Hang Tuah Jaya have announced their departure from the party, three days before polling in the Melaka election.
Former Bersatu Hang Tuah Jaya deputy division chief Md Firdaus Mashor said the decision was made collectively following discussions and agreement among the leadership and members.
The departure takes effect immediately today. Firdaus also resigned as Bersatu Melaka information secretary.
He said the group had also decided to vote for Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates in the state election and the next general election.
Speaking at a press conference at the Umno Hang Tuah Jaya division office in Bukit Katil today, Firdaus said one of the factors behind their decision was the Rumah Bangsa initiative introduced by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"We see this initiative as an inclusive approach that creates an opportunity to reunite Malays and Muslims who were previously divided by political differences, based on mutual understanding, respect and common interests," he said.
He said they had also considered the need for political stability, mature leadership and an administration focused on development and public welfare.
The group viewed Umno and BN as a more suitable platform for them to continue serving the public, particularly in the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary constituency.
Among those leaving Bersatu were several members of its Hang Tuah Jaya division committee, as well as leaders and members from several branches, including Padang Jambu, Batu Hampar, Pasir Puteh, Paya Dalam, Bukit Baru Dalam and Kandang.
They are voters in the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary constituency, particularly in the Pengkalan Batu and Ayer Molek state constituencies.
The announcement comes three days before polling day for the 16th Melaka election on Nov 14, with campaigning entering its final stretch.
Also present at the press conference were Hang Tuah Jaya Umno deputy division chief Datuk Hasnoor Sidang Hussin and Perikatan Nasional Bukit Katil candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid confident Negri Sembilan political impasse will be resolved soon
Article:
TANGGA BATU: The political and administrative impasse in Negri Sembilan is expected to be resolved soon through ongoing discussions involving the relevant parties, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid, who is also Umno president and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said efforts were underway to find a solution, potentially involving the party's central and state leadership, as well as the Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar.
He said the discussions would prioritise the interests of the people, particularly with the state budget due to be tabled soon.
"This is something we are working on. There is a possibility that the central Umno leadership, together with the Negri Sembilan Umno leadership and the menteri besar, will be involved in finding a solution.
"Our priority is to ensure that services to the people continue, especially with the state budget approaching.
"It would be impossible for the budget to be tabled without the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan," he told reporters after attending the BN-Perikatan Nasional grand finale speech for the Paya Rumput state constituency here tonight.
Zahid expressed confidence that the Negri Sembilan budget could be tabled this month, given the ongoing efforts to resolve the impasse.
He also hoped that the state legislative assembly sitting could proceed as planned and the budget be approved to ensure the smooth running of the state administration.
"Hopefully, once the Negri Sembilan state assembly proceedings are held and the budget is approved, administrative matters can be carried out with the cooperation of the state government.
"This includes the state secretary, legal adviser, state financial officer, district officers and officials at the sub-district level.
"I am confident that if we work towards finding a solution, we will eventually reach common ground and achieve the consensus needed to ensure Negri Sembilan is governed effectively," he said.
The constitutional and administrative crisis in Negri Sembilan, a state with a monarchy rooted in Minangkabau traditions, began in April this year.
The impasse is approaching a critical juncture as statutory deadlines for resolving the crisis draw nearer.
The Negri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly has yet to convene since the state election in early August amid the continuing dispute involving the state's royal institution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Meta, TikTok join Google in opposing Indonesia's proposed AI copyright rules
Article:
JAKARTA: Digital platforms Meta and TikTok joined Google on Wednesday in pushing back against proposed revisions to Indonesia's copyright law that would require digital platforms to pay publishers for displaying news content and set rules for AI.
If the bill is passed, Indonesia could become the first country in Southeast Asia to incorporate AI in its copyright law, as governments globally grapple with the impact of the technology on copyright rules, including the use of work created by humans to train AI models.
Agung Pamungkas, Google's Indonesia government affairs and public policy manager, told a parliamentary hearing that requiring tech platforms to pay compensation for showing links of news content from publishers would limit Indonesians' access to news.
Berni Moestafa, Meta's public policy head in Indonesia, said requiring platforms to pay compensation meant news "publishers could lose readership traffic as well as potential advertising and subscription revenue".
Directing readers to an article is different from reproducing or republishing the article itself, Berni added.
Reuters exclusively reported the planned revisions in July, citing a draft of the bill.
Separately, Noudhy Valdryno, TikTok's head of public policy in Indonesia, told lawmakers that disclosure requirements should not apply where AI is used only in an assistive capacity rather than to fully create content.
Noudhy urged lawmakers to preserve safe-harbour protections, saying platforms cannot reliably determine copyright ownership or licences. - REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US midterm results put pro-Israel powerhouse AIPAC on the defensive
Article:
For years, the pro-Israel lobbying group Aipac was a United States political juggernaut, but deepening voter disillusion over US-Israeli ties and wins by Israel-sceptic candidates in last week's midterm elections have left it reeling.
Candidates of all stripes long courted the American Israel Public Affairs Committee's support. But what was once an asset has become a liability in many races, as favourable opinions of Israel plummet over civilian deaths in Gaza and the costly Iran war.
In the Michigan Senate race, Aipac's once irresistible force ran into an immovable object.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed — who tapped into anger over US funding for Israel's military — faced Aipac-supported candidates in  the primary and general election, but emerged victorious to become the first Muslim
senator.
The tens of millions of dollars spent by an Aipac-affiliated group, the United Democracy Project, not only failed to beat El-Sayed, but they helped him boost his own messaging.
"To Aipac... Thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice," the Michigan politician said in his victory speech.
The tables flipped so completely that allies of El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers,  even asked the group to stop spending on him at one point.
"They definitely have become a liability," said Adam Wood, a veteran Democratic campaign strategist with City & State Public Affairs,  noting several campaigns he worked on in years past "coveted" Aipac's support.
Another Democratic Senate success story, James Talarico, won in Texas with a similar message of ending US funding for Israeli offensive weaponry and keeping distance from Aipac.
"I've never taken money from Aipac, and I'm not taking money from Aipac in this campaign," Talarico said early in his bid.
Officially, Aipac is non-partisan. It has traditionally supported candidates from  the left and the right.
According to its website, it only accepts money from Americans and its board is composed exclusively of Americans.
But the group has become a byword in US politics for Washington's tight ties with Israeli governments, including the outgoing far-right coalition of Benja-min Netanyahu.
The Chicago Council on Global Affairs has asked Americans to rate their favourability of Israel on a scale of 0 to 100 regularly since 1978 and this year marked a record low: an average score of just 44.
That's down from 58 in 2022, when the previous midterms were held.
And for Democrats, the numbers are all the starker: a drop in favourability from 52 in 2022 to just 30 today.
"Democrats started to really tank on Israel," said Dina Smeltz, a former State Department official who is now a managing director at the council.
Leftist Democratic star, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, has branded Aipac as "a right-wing organisation that undermines democracy".
But support also appears to be faltering on the right.
On election day, President Donald Trump dialled into his favourite morning programme,
Fox & Friends
, and made the surprising announcement that the US would be ending a major annual aid package to Israel — something El-Sayed and others on the left have repeatedly demanded.
Vice-President J.D. Vance said he'd been told by a trusted pollster that his party's road to recovery after the midterms annihilation will require, in part, changing "our relationship to Israel".
And other right-wing voices, including broadcaster Tucker Carlson and libertarian Representative Thomas Massie, have  criticised Israel in recent years in ways unimaginable in the 2000s and 2010s.
Pro-Israel lobbyists are not going to go away of course.
Aipac  has competition from the left-leaning pro-Israel J Street as well as the recently formed pro-Palestine American Priorities super PAC.
The aftermath of elections in Israel, with the possible political eclipse of Netanyahu, could also help Aipac to find its feet again.
"It has been around for a long time.  It has a lot of money," Smeltz said.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak rise to 1,435
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Selangor and Perak rose to 1,435 from 406 families, with nine temporary relief centres operating as of 10pm.
The figure was up from 1,359 evacuees from 391 families at eight relief centres recorded at 4.30pm.
The Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal said Selangor continued to record the highest number of evacuees, with 1,133 people from 319 families housed at seven relief centres in Kuala Selangor.
Perak recorded 302 evacuees from 87 families at two relief centres in Hilir Perak.
Of the total number of evacuees, 465 were adult women, 427 adult men, 214 girls and 288 boys.
Another 25 male babies and 16 female babies were also evacuated to the relief centres.

Title: Indonesia's Gibran quits as vice-president amid eligibility controversy
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned, an aide said on Wednesday, a move that threatens to split a key political alliance and risks further political uncertainty in Southeast Asia's largest economy.
Gibran, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, has come under intense scrutiny from lawmakers following Constitutional Court and Supreme Court rulings last month that his education documents did not meet election requirements.
The aide, Budi Arie Setiadi, told Reuters that Gibran had tendered his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto earlier on Wednesday.
Separately, two sources at the parliamentary upper house, which will oversee the process of approving his resignation and selecting a replacement, said that he would submit his resignation letter to the upper house on Thursday morning.
The resignation comes amid growing signs of strain in the political alliance between Prabowo, a powerful former general, and Widodo, also known as Jokowi, a highly popular leader who twice defeated Prabowo for the presidency before throwing him his support after facing term limits.
An open split could spark further instability for an administration hit by scandals over signature programmes, such as its free school meals policy, and doubts over its handling of the economy, political analysts say.
Investor sentiment has weakened towards Indonesia this year amid heightened scrutiny of the government's fiscal plans and its broader policy directions, as well as lingering downgrade risks for its stock market by global index provider MSCI.
Gibran's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Last week, Prabowo fired his chief of staff, widely seen as a Jokowi loyalist, after he was arrested on accusations of bugging the president, among other figures.
CALLS FOR IMPEACHMENT
Gibran stated his intention to resign during a meeting with Prabowo on Tuesday.
The parliamentary upper house will have to convene a session to declare a vacancy following the submission of Gibran's resignation letter, while writing a letter to the president requesting that he submit two names for his replacement, said senior law minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra.
After that, the upper house would hold an election within 60 days.
Earlier on Wednesday, some 120 Indonesian lawmakers from across the political spectrum submitted a petition demanding Gibran's impeachment, fuelling tensions around his political future.
Gibran "no longer meets the requirements as vice president as stipulated in Indonesia's constitution," said Mardani Ali Sera, one of the lawmakers who signed the petition.
ELIGIBILITY QUESTIONS
Gibran faced complaints over whether his education credentials met legal requirements, and on Tuesday the Supreme Court said it was instructing the education ministry to withdraw Gibran's education equivalence certificate, which the court has annulled.
Gibran, who studied abroad, used the certificate to comply with education requirements and run in the 2024 election, which he won alongside Prabowo.
Indonesian election law requires vice-presidential candidates to have completed senior high ​school or an equivalent level of education, but the court found that the certificate was issued based on evidence that did not actually prove Jokowi's eldest son had graduated.
"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," the court said in the ruling.
The Supreme Court also took into account the Constitutional Court's ruling, which said Gibran's education documents did not meet election requirements.
Gibran's spot on the 2024 ticket was previously marred by ethics complaints after the Constitutional Court, headed at the time by his uncle, removed an age limit that would have prevented his candidacy.
Sana Jaffrey, a ⁠researcher at the Australian National University, said the crisis showed how the political fortunes of a small number of elites took precedence over the country's need for effective and stable governance.
"Prolonged uncertainty at the highest levels of power will only deepen anxieties at home and abroad about where the country is headed," she said.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing sailors expose human cost of Iran war at sea
Article:
V. Pandiselvi, the mother of Indian sailor Naveen Kumar, has not heard from her son for more than six months yet she still clings to hope he will return, crying as she replays old voice notes.
Kumar was one of six crew members on two Iran-linked cargo vessels last seen in Iranian waters in May before disappearing.
Commercial ships have come under fire since the United States and Israel's  war on Iran began on Feb 28.
Teheran attacked ships to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz and the US in turn struck Iran-linked ships to impose a blockade on Iranian ports.
The United Nations' International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has confirmed 130 "incidents" —  mainly attacks —  in the region since the conflict began, with at least 25 seafarers killed.
"We cannot bear this pain," Pandiselvi, 45, said from her one-bedroom house in the city of Dindigul in southern India's Tamil Nadu state.
"You don't need anyone to tell you what  parents would go through if they were to lose their child. We appeal to everyone involved to  help us."
Reuters spoke to shipping sources, Iraqi officials and the families of missing sailors in Iraq's Basra and India's Tamil Nadu state to reveal the human cost of Hormuz attacks.
The 23-year-old Kumar's family took on considerable debt for him to complete a marine course and pursue his dream of working as a sailor, after which he left for a six-month crew contract he was told was based in Dubai.
A week in, he found himself in Iran. Even before war broke out three months later, Kumar's family was desperately trying to repatriate him. Then came radio silence.
"Is he still on that ship, or has something terrible happened to him?
"It's causing a lot of confusion. Every passing minute is agony," Pandiselvi said.
Kumar had been deployed to the vessels
Bridge 1
and
Bridge 2
, which disappeared around May 9. The two ships were not on the IMO's list of incidents.
Iraq said in May it was monitoring the disappearance of the two vessels, which flew the Bolivian flag. No distress signals were received.
Khaled Saad al-Thaalibi, who heads the Iraqi maritime foundation in Basra, said the latest available information indicated the vessels' Automatic Identification System (AIS) transmitted their last known position approximately 8 nautical miles from Iran's Kish Island on May 9 at 4.50pm.
"We called the agent in Iran but he told us that he knew nothing about the incident and on the following day the Iranian search and rescue tried to look for the vessels but they found nothing," Thaalibi said from his office in Basra.
The other
Bridge 1
and
2
crew members missing are three Iraqis, one Pakistani and another Indian.
Haider Rahman al-Mayahi, a 22-year-old Iraqi sailor, was on the crew, his brother Youssef Rahman said.
"He left behind a 1-year-old daughter and a father who suffered a stroke from the grief of his disappearance."
Al-Mayahi's family travelled to Iran seeking answers.
They located the vessels' owner, an Iranian who told them he had no information on the vessels.
The family received conflicting theories about the vessels.
Some shipping sources said they may have been struck by the US and sunk immediately while others speculated the crew had been detained by a Gulf state or Iran.
An order dated May 22, published on a government website, showed India's Seamen's Employment Office withdrew the recruitment licence of Lascar Marine Services and barred its past and present directors from maritime business for five years, citing repeated failures to repatriate seafarers — including Kumar — or pay their wages.
Since the Iran war, costs of hiring sailors have tripled with many working just one journey as risks mount.
A captain, the highest paid crew member on a vessel, could make  US$8,000 to US$13,000 a month before the conflict. Now they can earn three times that.
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't dissolve Parliament over cabinet reshuffle, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parliament should not be dissolved simply because of questions surrounding a cabinet reshuffle when the government remains functional and commands majority support, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh.
She said that after nearly four years of the Unity Government, the country should be able to focus on more pressing priorities, including investment, job opportunities, the cost of living and the long-standing institutional reform agenda.
"That is why I believe the proposal to dissolve Parliament when the government is still functioning and has majority support should not be raised lightly, especially when the original issue concerns only a cabinet reshuffle.
"A cabinet reshuffle is part of the process of strengthening the administration. It should not be used as a reason to reopen an episode of political uncertainty that we have experienced before," she said in a Facebook post today.
The Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general said the political instability between 2020 and 2022, when the country was grappling with the Covid-19 pandemic, job losses and cost-of-living pressures, should serve as a lesson on the importance of maintaining a stable government.
She said efforts to strengthen governance, combat corruption and improve national institutions required policy continuity and a stable administration to ensure that the benefits reached the people.
Differences of opinion among leaders, she added, could be discussed without undermining the stability the country was working to build.
Fuziah also cautioned against allowing political interests to take precedence over the nation's future and the well-being of the people, who had long borne the consequences of political uncertainty.
Recently, certain quarters have called for Parliament to be dissolved instead of proceeding with a cabinet reshuffle, following the impending end of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan's term as a Dewan Negara member on Dec 11.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan: Loke's resignation a big loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has described Anthony Loke as a principled man, saying his resignation as transport minister was a big loss.
Ramanan said any cabinet reshuffle was for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to decide.
"I am sad. He is my good friend and cabinet colleague. I will miss him.
"But this is his decision and his stand. He is a very principled man. We have to accept it. It is a big loss," he told reporters on the sidelines of the Social Security Organisation Media Awards 2026 tonight.
Loke
resigned as transport minister
with immediate effect yesterday following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.
DAP had previously said discussions on a
replacement for Loke
were premature.
Anwar said yesterday that it was
too early to discuss
a cabinet reshuffle.

Title: Selangor shuts waterfall areas over safety concerns
Article:
SHAH ALAM: All waterfall recreational areas in permanent forest reserves in Selangor have been closed with immediate effect until further notice due to unpredictable weather conditions.
The Selangor Forestry Department said the closure was ordered on safety grounds as changing weather conditions could increase risks to visitors.
"The public are prohibited from entering the closed waterfall areas or carrying out any recreational activities at these locations while the closure order remains in force.
"Legal action may be taken against anyone who defies the closure order," it said in a statement posted on Facebook today.
The department also advised the public to comply with the order and avoid visiting waterfall recreational areas to protect themselves and their families.
Further information on the closure is available on the department's official website at
www.forestry.selangor.gov.my
.
The closure comes amid heightened safety concerns following a water surge at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Baru on Nov 9, which swept away eight people.
Five bodies have been recovered, while three people remained missing as of Nov 11. Another 26 people who were stranded near the river were rescued.
The Fire and Rescue Department has advised the public to postpone water-based recreational activities, including swimming, bathing, picnicking and camping at rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals throughout the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon season.
It warned that unpredictable weather and prolonged heavy rain could cause sudden rises in water levels, strong currents and water surges.

Title: NST Leader: Malaysia's zero-waste ambition needs funding, action and accountability
Article:
The multi-pronged environmental reforms Malaysia proposed at COP31 in Türkiye to advance its zero-waste agenda will be challenging to implement, both logistically and financially.
First, urban circularity, which involves recovering, repairing, reusing and recycling materials, can protect supply chains from global disruptions while creating jobs in repair and waste sorting.
While minimising greenhouse gas emissions is essential, exploiting natural resources is still cheaper.
Then there's the risk of allowing hazardous, outdated additives to circulate  indefinitely.
Second, tracking materials digitally can identify waste chemistry and hold manufacturers accountable under extended producer responsibility laws.
However, small businesses and the informal waste sector may be unable to absorb the high compliance costs.
Moreover, tracking loses its effectiveness once materials cross international borders.
Third, municipal financing ties capital to environmental metrics, preventing greenwashing and motivating city councils to reach  goals.
While urban waste programmes can secure incentives, underfunded districts may lag behind.
Fourth, equitable resource redistribution and the zero-waste agenda require wealthy nations to transfer technology, expertise and funding to developing cities struggling with mounting waste.
However, such transfers often depend on voluntary commitments or international agreements, which can falter when they conflict with national economic priorities.
How monumental is the cost? On a global scale, the transition to a circular economy will unlock US$4.5 trillion in  economic value by 2030.
Last year, Malaysia generated 14.5 million  tonnes of municipal solid waste, costing the government RM2 billion annually.
So, yes, Malaysia may immediately feel the impact of  skyrocketing municipal waste because closing a fully loaded, non-sanitary landfill site costs RM20 million.
To support the Circular Economy Blueprint for Solid Waste (2025–2035), which targets a recycling rate of 40 per cent, the government will depend heavily on private-sector green investment.
As of mid-2025, this sector attracted RM22.7 billion in investments.
Diverting waste saves parts of the RM2 billion  annual maintenance bill, avoids RM20 million landfill closure penalties and grows the national circular economy gross value added  to RM20 billion.
Malaysia's proposals are welcome but their value depends on practical improvements in people's lives.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming, who led the Malaysian delegation, called for 20 per cent of urban climate financing to go to local authorities and communities.
This will  provide funding and technical capacity to  protect vulnerable communities and informal settlements.
Climate adaptation must not become a privilege for wealthy neighbourhoods.    While local authorities need empowerment, they must also be held accountable for progress.
Nga's initiatives deserve  consideration and concrete action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Policeman seriously injured in parang attack at Kepong apartment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A policeman was seriously injured after being attacked with a sharp weapon by a man at an apartment in Desa Jaya, Kepong, today.
The policeman was believed to have been attacked while a team was conducting an operation at one of the apartment units. However, details of the incident have yet to be confirmed.
A video circulating on social media showed a man attacking an individual believed to be a policeman with two parangs. The victim reportedly sustained serious injuries to his right hand.
The media is seeking confirmation and further details from police, including the victim's condition and the suspect's identity.

Title: Perkeso told to expedite benefits for injured journalists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has directed the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) to expedite benefits for two journalists injured in a road accident in Perak.
The journalists, from the New Straits Times and Bernama, were involved in the crash on Oct 25.
Speaking at the  Perkeso Media Awards 2026 gathering, Ramanan said journalists often worked in difficult conditions to ensure accurate reporting.
"To me, matters like this cannot be taken lightly because social protection must reach those who truly need it," he said.
"Sometimes in the rain, journalists have to be there," he added.
He said Perkeso would provide the necessary protection to journalists.
"Based on the social protection we have, whatever is needed, I will make sure [Perkeso] provides it for all of you," he said.
New Straits Times journalist Zahratulhayat Md Arif, 37, and Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, were injured when
their car was rear-ended by a lorry
in Ipoh.

Title: NSTP sweeps top honours at Perkeso Media Awards 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd (NSTP) emerged among the top winners at the Perkeso I Lindung U Media Awards 2026, securing several honours for impactful journalism.
The highlight was NST Life and Times editor Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal, who won the Kencana Kesuma Perkeso Lindung Semua Award, the top honour recognising outstanding journalism with a positive impact on public awareness of social protection.
In the Best Print Media Report category, Harian Metro journalist Mohd Alhafiz Ithnin clinched first place.
The achievement was further marked by Berita Harian journalists Suzalina Halid and Latifah Arifin, who secured second place in the same category.
The Perkeso I Lindung U Media Awards 2026 recognise media practitioners who consistently deliver accurate information and raise public awareness of the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) role in safeguarding people's welfare.
Meanwhile, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Kencana Kesuma Perkeso award was given to the best work among all entries.
He said it represented the highest recognition for work that excelled not only in journalistic quality but also in its impact on society.
"Such recognition is certainly an appreciation of the efforts and work produced by our media colleagues," he said.

Title: 400k Malaysia-Singapore commuters to benefit from social security amendment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An amendment that will benefit about 400,000 workers who commute daily between Malaysia and Singapore will be passed before the end of the year, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said.
A separate amendment introducing a post-maternity leave allowance for more than 132,000 women workers will also go before Parliament before the new year, he said.
The first amendment is to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017 (Act 789).
"We will make sure this is passed before we celebrate the new year, before the Parliament sitting closes," Ramanan said at the Social Security Organisation Media Awards 2026 night.
He said the second amendment, to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800), concerned the post-maternity leave allowance.
"It is expected to benefit more than 132,000 women workers," he said.
Ramanan said both initiatives reflected the Madani government's efforts, through the Human Resources Ministry, to strengthen social protection and safeguard workers' welfare.
Also present were Social Security Organisation chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal, its chief executive Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed, and Media Prima Bhd chief operating officer Datuk Mohd Effendy Othman.
In June, Ramanan said the
proposal for the Traveller Scheme
, which provides social protection for Malaysians working abroad, particularly in Singapore, was in its final stages ahead of implementation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan lauds media for taking government policies to millions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has praised journalists for their role in bringing government policies and initiatives to the public.
He said more than 40,000 media reports on his ministry's work had been published since he took office on Dec 12.
"You play a very important role as the link between the government and the people, delivering information responsibly and ethically," he said at the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Media Awards 2026 tonight.
Describing the coverage as a proud achievement, he said it demonstrated the media's important role in disseminating information to the public.
Ramanan said journalists helped take government announcements far beyond the venues where they were made.
"If I speak in a hall like this, there may be 500 people, but because of the friends here, millions will know.
"It's a very big duty and a very big task. So I understand, it's not an easy job, but all of you are capable and you are doing a fantastic job," he said.
He said the Kencana Award, introduced for the first time this year, would recognise the best entry across all categories and represent the highest recognition for journalism with the greatest impact on society.
The New Straits Times' Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal won the inaugural Kencana Award.
Ramanan also highlighted Perkeso chief executive Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed's position as president of the International Social Security Association, saying the appointment required votes from 165 countries.
"What we do in the Social Security Organisation is not first class in Malaysia.
"It is first class in the world, it is world class," he said.
The minister also paid tribute to the late Makkal Osai senior editor Dr Rajan Gopal, who had served 50 years in journalism, including 15 years with the newspaper.
Also present were Perkeso chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Media Prima Bhd chief operating officer Datuk Mohd Effendy Othman.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pope draws huge crowds at Argentina shrine before Peru homecoming
Article:
LUJÁN: Pope Leo XIV drew vast crowds to Argentina's holiest shrine Wednesday, the final day of his visit before he departs for Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.
Authorities said two million people packed the streets around the Basilica of Lujan, with some climbing fences, barriers, trees and lampposts for a glimpse of the pontiff as crowds chanted "thank you Leo for your blessing."
The stop at Lujan is the emotional centerpiece of Leo's first visit to Argentina, where his predecessor Francis never returned home as pope.
"This is a very important moment for us, we had an Argentine pope and he wasn't able to come, that hurt me," said 76-year-old Estela Adorno.
The 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru less than a month after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.
The South America tour has been cast as a double homecoming, bringing Leo to Argentina, birthplace of Francis, before taking him to Peru, where he spent years as a missionary and church leader before becoming pope.
Throughout his stay in Argentina, Leo has pointedly urged leaders to build a more inclusive economy and protect society's most vulnerable, comments widely interpreted as criticism of President Javier Milei's government.
Those social concerns were visible in the crowd at Lujan. One group unfurled a banner reading "land, housing and work for the people," while a woman held a sign calling for the release of a man she said had been wrongly imprisoned.
Adorno said the pope's message had resonated in a country marked by political and economic divisions.
"Everything that helps society is welcome. People were deeply moved, I was deeply moved. With everything that is happening in the country, it will always be welcome," she added.
- FLOURISHING THROUGH LIMITS -
Volunteers handed out water in the crowd as pilgrims continued streaming into Lujan under the spring sun.
Inside the basilica, choir members prepared for a Mass they described as a once-in-a-lifetime occasion.
"It is a unique opportunity, full of emotion. From the moment we were told we would participate, through preparing the repertoire and these final days of rehearsals, there has been so much shared excitement," said choir member Nora Jauregui, a 61-year-old retired music teacher.
Earlier Wednesday, Leo visited inmates at Buenos Aires' Devoto prison, where he urged prisoners to use their time behind bars as an opportunity to rebuild their lives.
"Human beings often flourish through limits rather than despite them," the pope told around 75 inmates and family members gathered in the prison gymnasium.
He acknowledged the hardship of prison life, saying he could imagine their sleepless nights and thoughts of loved ones or those they may have harmed.
The US-born pope had refused to reschedule the trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru despite having the lower part of his right lung removed to extract a cancerous tumour. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian Bar challenges legality of Najib's house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar has filed a legal challenge to Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest arrangement, arguing that it is unconstitutional and has no basis in law.
The legal body has applied to the High Court for leave to quash the Federal Territories Pardons Board's proceedings and decisions relating to the arrangement granted on Sept 18.
It is also seeking a stay of its implementation, pending the disposal of the judicial review, if leave is granted.
The application names the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Prisons Commissioner-General and Najib as respondents.
In an affidavit filed yesterday, Bar secretary Jayabalan Raman Kutty said the application concerned important principles of constitutional and fundamental rights.
In its accompanying statement, the Bar argued that house arrest did not fall within the meaning of a pardon, reprieve or respite under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"The intended 'House Arrest' for Najib does not fall within the meaning of a pardon, a reprieve, or a respite; conditional or otherwise.
"It is not permitted by the Constitution. It is ultra vires the Constitution," it said.
The Bar argued that house arrest was not provided for under Malaysian criminal law and that the arrangement appeared to have been specifically tailored for Najib.
It claimed that this contravened Article 8 of the Federal Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law.
The legal body also questioned whether the Pardons Board had exhausted its authority over the matter after granting Najib a partial pardon in January 2024.
The decision reduced his SRC International prison sentence from 12 years to six and his fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.
The Bar argued that allowing house arrest on top of the earlier reduction was improper and disproportionate to the seriousness of his crimes and their continuing consequences for the country.
It also claimed that the board had failed to adequately consider relevant factors, including Najib's other conviction and prison sentence, the financial burden of his crimes and their impact on public confidence in anti-corruption efforts.
The Bar further alleged that his application lacked any acceptance of guilt, contrition or remorse and instead challenged the outcome of the judicial process.
Among the orders sought are declarations that the house arrest arrangement, along with measures taken by the minister and Prisons Commissioner-General to facilitate it, are unlawful, unconstitutional, null and void.
The Bar also wants Najib barred from submitting further pardon applications until all his pending criminal cases have been finally disposed of and he publicly accepts responsibility and expresses remorse.
It is seeking a corresponding order preventing the board from considering such applications until those conditions are met.
Najib began serving his SRC International sentence on Aug 23, 2022, after exhausting his appeals.
Yesterday, the High Court ordered him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, following a conditional pardon and full payment of his RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 foreigners rob man of RM10k at Penang petrol station
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Four foreigners injured a 43-year-old man and robbed him of RM10,000 at a petrol station in Permatang Pauh after posing as donation seekers.
Police said the suspects were believed to be from Central Asia. No further details were provided.
Police are tracking down the two men and two women involved in the robbery.
Seberang Prai Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incident occurred at 11.30am yesterday at the entrance to a BHPetrol station along Jalan Samagagah.
Initial investigations found that the suspects solicited monetary donations from members of the public before turning aggressive.
"They used a sharp iron object to injure the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings," he said in a statement today.
Total losses were estimated at RM10,000.
Nik Aminuddin said the case is being investigated under Section 394 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt in committing a robbery.
Police advised the public to remain vigilant against such tactics and contact the Penang police control centre at 04-222 1722 or 04-269 1999 if they needed assistance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RON97 drops 50 sen, unsubsidised RON95 down 40 sen, diesel 25 sen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of RON97 will drop by 50 sen per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 will fall by 40 sen and unsubsidised diesel by 25 sen, effective tomorrow until Nov 18.
The new prices are RM4.20 per litre for RON97, RM3.87 for RON95 and RM4.87 for diesel.
The Finance Ministry said in a statement today that prices of refined petroleum products in regional markets had declined during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, in line with lower global crude oil prices and increased supplies of refined fuel in regional markets.
However, it said global petroleum prices remained vulnerable to significant fluctuations as long as the conflict in Iran remained unresolved, while recent attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz showed that the risk of supply disruptions persisted.
"The government remains committed to protecting the people and businesses through the implementation of targeted fuel subsidies under Budi Madani.
"As announced in the 2027 Budget, fuel subsidies are expected to remain high at around RM40 billion next year to help ease the cost-of-living pressures," it said.
Under Budi95, eligible recipients continue to enjoy RON95 at RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM3.87. The government bears a subsidy of RM1.88 per litre, equivalent to 49 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
For Budi Diesel, eligible recipients continue to pay RM2.10 per litre compared with the unsubsidised price of RM4.87, with the government absorbing RM2.77 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
"The subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged, with RON95 under Budi95 at RM1.99 per litre; diesel under Budi Diesel at RM2.10 per litre; the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) at RM2.05 per litre; and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) at RM2.15 per litre.
"Through Budi95 and Budi Diesel, eligible Malaysians can continue purchasing subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to the monthly eligibility limits," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah hospital separates conjoined twins in second successful surgery
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah has successfully performed its second separation surgery on conjoined twins, bringing forward the operation after one of the babies required increasing respiratory support.
The premature male twins, classified as pygopagus, were joined at the lower spine, sacrum and pelvis. They underwent the complex procedure at Sabah Women and Children's Hospital in Likas.
They were delivered through an emergency Caesarean section at 32 weeks of gestation after the condition was detected during routine antenatal care, and were admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) for monitoring.
The hospital initially planned to separate the twins when they were four to six months old to allow them to grow and stabilise. However, the operation was brought forward after one twin required increasing respiratory support in the NICU.
The medical and surgical teams decided to proceed on the 40th day after birth, taking into account the physiological strain on their shared organ systems, the hospital said in a statement on its Facebook page.
The procedure involved separating their connected lower intestinal and urinary systems, followed by reconstruction of the pelvic floor, creation of a neoanus and restoration of the urinary pathways.
The operation required close coordination among multidisciplinary teams from Sabah Women and Children's Hospital, Hospital Tunku Azizah in Kuala Lumpur and Hospital Umum Sarawak.
The hospital said performing the high-risk procedure in Sabah strengthened the state's specialised paediatric healthcare capabilities and avoided the need to transfer the premature babies by air to Peninsular Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians arrested in Mauritius over RM9mil cannabis haul knew they carried drugs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysians arrested in Mauritius with 76.14kg of cannabis worth RM9.87 million knowingly transported the drugs after collecting them in Bangkok, police said.
Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the trio, comprising a couple and another individual recruited through a holiday package, knew they were carrying drugs.
He said investigations had established that the suspects travelled from Malaysia to Bangkok, where they collected the drugs before continuing their journey to Mauritius.
"What we know for certain is that they travelled from Malaysia to Bangkok.
"They collected the drug supply in Bangkok before taking it to Mauritius.
"They knew what they were carrying," he told reporters at an appreciation ceremony for NCID's Intelligence and Operations Division.
Hussein said Malaysian authorities had received information from their counterparts in Mauritius to facilitate further investigations locally.
"We have been provided with the relevant information for us to conduct further investigations here," he said.
The three Malaysians, comprising 2 men aged 22 and 30 and an 18-year-old woman,
were arrested
upon arrival at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport on Nov 2.
According to the Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA), customs officers discovered 70 rectangular, vacuum-packed parcels containing suspected cannabis in their luggage. The drugs were valued at 114.21 million Mauritian rupees (RM9.87 million).
Mauritius media reported that the 30-year-old suspect, who worked as a security officer in Singapore, was carrying 10.9kg of cannabis, while the 22-year-old man and 18-year-old woman were found with 32.5kg and 32.6kg respectively.
Preliminary investigations by Mauritian authorities had linked the drugs to Thailand, with reports indicating that at least one suspect had travelled through Dubai before arriving in Mauritius.
The arrests came just 10 days after another Malaysian, a 55-year-old cook, was detained at the same airport on Oct 23 with 17.8kg of cannabis in his luggage after arriving from Dubai.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's daughter conveys his message to Melaka voters ahead of polls
Article:
MELAKA: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's daughter, Nooryana Najwa, better known as Yana Najib, said her father had a message for the people of Melaka ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.
She said her father wanted to remind voters that Barisan Nasional was the coalition best placed to secure their future, particularly that of the younger generation.
"Datuk Seri Najib has always hoped for a BN victory. He is someone who is deeply committed to the party.
"He understands the sacrifices involved in politics and has always advised me and my brothers to engage with the people and help them.
"There was no specific message, but he wanted to tell the people of Melaka that BN is the best party to secure the future of the younger generation," she said.
She was speaking to reporters after attending the meet-and-greet with the Asahan Community programme here today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NCID seeks 1,000 more personnel to target drug syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) is seeking 1,000 additional positions to strengthen intelligence and enforcement operations against major drug syndicates amid manpower shortages.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the proposal had received Cabinet approval in principle last month and required further discussions with the Public Service Department before the positions could be finalised.
He said the additional manpower would strengthen the department's Intelligence and Operations Division, whose undercover operatives gathered intelligence, identified syndicate networks and supported major enforcement operations.
"Without the Intelligence and Operations Division, we would not be able to build major cases. We would only be arresting drug addicts or street-level pushers," he said.
Hussein was speaking to reporters at an appreciation ceremony for the division, which recognised partner agencies and companies that had assisted police in operations, raids, seizures and arrests.
He said the dismantling of a major clandestine drug laboratory in Puncak Alam several months ago as an example of the division's role.
The operation, which involved drugs worth billions of ringgit, required months of intelligence gathering before investigators identified the facility and determined when to strike.
Hussein said NCID had recorded seizures totalling nearly 70 tonnes of drugs in the first 10 months of this year, compared with 89 tonnes throughout last year.
He said more needed to be done to disrupt drug supplies and dismantle trafficking networks.
"As long as we do not cripple these syndicate networks, drugs will continue to be available in the market," he said.
The additional positions would also support specialised units focusing on online investigations, international drug trafficking, courier services and containerised cargo.
Hussein said a dedicated international investigations unit was needed to handle increasingly complex cases involving private jets, vessels and cross-border trafficking networks.
He said specialised teams were also needed to monitor courier services and container movements, which were being exploited by drug traffickers.
The proposed expansion would strengthen NCID's capabilities at district, state and federal levels, allowing it to conduct more operations and dismantle more syndicates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Najib's house arrest should not be election campaign material
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has reminded all parties against using the issue of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest as campaign material in the Melaka election.
He said political leaders, particularly those holding ministerial positions, should not involve the public in campaigning on the matter.
"Granting a pardon is the absolute prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay Rulers. Whatever our views may be, that prerogative cannot be questioned.
"The matter is enshrined in the Federal Constitution. As such, questioning it would mean questioning the country's Constitution.
"As ministers, we must respect the Constitution because it forms the foundation of our nation. We must not undermine it, as doing so could harm the country," he said.
Mohamad, fondly known as Tok Mat, was commenting on DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's call for Melaka voters dissatisfied with the decision on Najib's house arrest to express their views through the ballot box.
He said the issue should not be used as campaign material, adding that political leaders must understand the limits of what could be raised.
"Do not use this matter as a campaign tool. We must know what can and cannot be discussed.
"Granting a pardon is an absolute prerogative. Anyone may express their views, but we cannot question the absolute prerogative of the Malay Rulers.
"The matter is enshrined in the Constitution. I hope Najib's house arrest will not be used as campaign material. He has not been released; instead, the house has been gazetted as a prison," he said after meeting members of the Durian Tunggal community here today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Wan Azizah convey condolences over Melaka PKR leader J. Samivel’s passing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail have extended their condolences to the family of Alor Gajah PKR branch vice-chief J. Samivel, who died in a road accident in Jasin earlier today.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said in a Facebook post today that Samivel, 62, was also the representative for P. Denesh, the PH candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka state election.
“Samivel had served the party for many years and remained steadfast in its struggle. May his contributions and spirit continue to guide us as we carry on this struggle.
“My thoughts and prayers, together with Azizah, are with his family and comrades. May they be given strength and fortitude in facing this difficult trial,” he said.
Jasin police chief Supt Lee Robert said police received a report about the accident involving the car Samivel was travelling in at Jalan Pondok Batang, Jasin, at about 12.45 pm today. — Bernama

Title: Cabinet to be briefed on latest constitutional amendments separating AG, Public Prosecutor roles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11— The Parliamentary Special Select Committee (JKPK) on Constitutional Amendments Relating to the Separation of the Roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor has decided that the latest proposed amendments to the Federal Constitution on the reform be brought to the Cabinet’s attention.
In a statement today, the committee said the decision was made after hearing a presentation and feedback from the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) on the proposed amendments, following its review of matters raised at the 270th Meeting of the Conference of Rulers.
“The committee examined the proposed amendments submitted by the AGC, particularly to ensure that the matters raised by the Conference of Rulers receive due consideration in strengthening the legal framework for implementing the reform, in line with the principles of constitutional monarchy and the supremacy of the Federal Constitution,” the statement said.
The committee also reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that the separation of the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor is implemented carefully and in accordance with the Constitution to strengthen the independence of the prosecution institution, accountability and public confidence in the country’s justice system.
The meeting was chaired by Pengerang Member of Parliament, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Also present were Parit Sulong MP and Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, William Leong Jee Keen (Selayang), Syahredzan Johan (Bangi), Ramkarpal Singh (Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Beluran), Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (Kota Bharu) and Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muar).
Larut MP and Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, Alor Gajah MP and Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Datuk Lo Su Fui (Tawau) and Roy Angau Gingkoi (Lubok Antu) were unable to attend the meeting due to unavoidable circumstances. — Bernama

Title: Nine-year-old boy killed in suspected crocodile attack in Kudat
Article:
KUDAT, Nov 11 — A nine-year-old boy was killed in a suspected crocodile attack while trying to retrieve a fishing hook caught in Sungai Semayan, Kampung Semayan, Pulau Banggi, today.
The victim, identified as Mohamad Hilmi Nurjahid, was a Year Three pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan Semayan.
Kudat District Police Chief Supt Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the incident occurred at about 3.30pm while the boy was fishing with his elder brother.
He said the boy went into the river to free his fishing hook but subsequently disappeared, believed to have been snatched by a crocodile.
A search and rescue operation involving police, Civil Defence Force personnel and villagers was launched after a report was received at about 4.30pm.
The boy was found by his father at about 8.10pm beneath Sungai Semayan Bridge, not far from where he was last seen.

Title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s leap to 27th globally in digital, AI competitiveness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Malaysia has climbed seven rungs to 27th place out of 70 economies in the IMD World Digital and AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 from 34th place last year, becoming the second-highest-ranked country in ASEAN after Singapore.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was driven particularly by a 21-place improvement in artificial intelligence (AI) adoption to 14th place globally, a 10-place improvement in efficiency to 28th place, and Malaysia’s implementation of the national AI strategy, which ranked 12th.
“Malaysia also ranks 18th in workforce development, second globally in graduates in sciences, fifth in venture capital, sixth in high-tech exports and eighth in investment incentives for AI.
“The Malaysia Digital Action Plan 2030 and the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (AI Nation 2030) aim to create up to 300,000 new AI-related jobs and contribute up to an additional 1.2 percentage points to gross domestic product (GDP) growth by 2030,” he said in a post on his official Facebook account today.
He added that under Budget 2027, RM30 million has been allocated through the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises integrate AI and automate their operations.
The allocation will also support the training and certification of 5,000 AI professionals, as well as provide an additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions for youth.
The IMD WDAIR 2026 by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD) evaluates 70 economies based on 88 criteria across five key factors: governance, technology and infrastructure, efficiency, workforce Development, and values. — Bernama

Title: Stay away from 14 Hulu Selangor rivers, waterfalls amid water surge danger, Fire Dept warns; Pertak, Siling, Batang Kali top hotspots
Article:
HULU SELANGOR, Nov 11 — Fourteen recreational areas in Hulu Selangor have been identified as high-risk locations for water surges, with Sungai Pertak, Sungai Siling and Sungai Batang Kali emerging as the three main hotspots.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said Sungai Batang Kali recorded four water surge incidents this year, followed by Sungai Siling with three and Sungai Pertak with two.
“Of the nine incidents recorded at these three locations, only the one at Sungai Pertak involved victims, while the others did not result in any casualties,” he told Bernama at the JBPM Forward Control Post at Jambatan Pertak here today.
He said the other 11 high-risk locations were Lata Medang in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Inki in Kalumpang, River View Sungai Bernam in Hulu Selangor, Sungai Sendat and Sungai Tua in Ulu Yam, Sungai Kedondong in Batang Kali, Sungai Cilin in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Pinang in Batang Kali, Air Terjun Serendah in Serendah, Air Terjun Semangkuk and Sungai Liam in Hulu Selangor.
In view of the north-east monsoon, Ashrul Riezal advised the public to temporarily suspend water-based recreational activities to avoid untoward incidents.
He said the advisory was aimed at raising awareness among local communities and visitors about the dangers of sudden water surges, particularly amid unpredictable weather conditions.
Eight people, comprising one Malaysian and seven foreigners, were swept away by strong currents during a water surge at Sungai Pertak at about 5.30pm last Monday.
Five were found drowned, including Malaysian V. Vijayan, 36, Nepalese national Kapali, 49, and Indian national B. Kunjanmalayil, 35. The identities of the other two, an Indian and a Sri Lankan, are being established.
The search continues for the remaining three victims, comprising two Indian nationals and a Yemeni. — Bernama

Title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements.
“Since the house (Najib’s residence) falls under the jurisdiction of the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD), I have instructed the IPD to conduct inspections and provide security monitoring from time to time,” he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating at the 2026 PDRM Integrity Month celebration here today.
Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.
Yesterday, Najib began serving the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest after the High Court here ruled that the order should take effect immediately.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the decision after setting aside an order issued by the High Court Criminal Registry on November 6 against Najib, 73. — AFP

Title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the decision, made at the Cabinet meeting on Nov 6, followed a surge in global crude palm oil (CPO) prices, which had significantly increased production costs for manufacturers.
“Through this mechanism, we can maintain the existing ceiling prices for 1kg, 2kg, 3kg and 5kg bottles, while providing special incentives to manufacturers producing bottled cooking oil,” he told a media conference held in conjunction with the 22nd Annual General Meeting of the Malaysian Muslim Restaurant Owners Association (PRESMA) here today.
He said based on the average global CPO price of RM4,400 per tonne in October 2026, the price of a 5kg bottle of cooking oil could have risen to RM34 without the intervention.
Under the mechanism, the ceiling prices of bottled pure palm cooking oil will remain at RM6.90 for 1kg, RM13.30 for 2kg, RM19.60 for 3kg and RM30.90 for 5kg, as stipulated under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011.
Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil.
He said the ministry (KPDN) had worked with the Finance Ministry and other relevant ministries to implement the mechanism as an intervention to ease cost-of-living pressures amid global market disruptions caused by the conflict in West Asia.
Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.
He also hoped the government would consider introducing targeted subsidies for restaurant operators in the future, similar to the assistance provided to manufacturers. — Bernama

Title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month.
Mohamad Imran Taj Maloor, 32, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan.
No plea was recorded from the accused, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years and, where the death penalty is not imposed, not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Vivi Asnita Zaina’Larifin, while the accused was represented by lawyer Azleen Farahannis.
No bail was allowed, and the court set January 28 next year for mention.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.
“As a result of the collision, the lorry veered onto the left road shoulder while its driver, a 39-year-old Indonesian man, suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene,” he said.
According to Mohd Zamzuri, an EBA II breath test recorded a blood alcohol reading of 61 mg/100ml for the car driver, while his passenger recorded 67 mg/100ml. — Bernama
