Title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation.
“From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.
She said the pace of modern development must not outstrip governance standards and constitutional guarantees.
Azalina said the completion of major infrastructure projects, including railways, industrial hubs and highways, should not be the sole measure of success, as the government must also ensure that the institutions entrusted with such powers exercised them responsibly and in accordance with the law.
She said physical progress alone did not define a country’s stature, stressing that while buildings might transform a nation’s skyline, the rule of law defined its character.
Meanwhile, she commended the legal fraternity for publishing academic and practical works that enriched jurisprudence and provided guidance to future legal practitioners. — Bernama

Title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL).
Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims.
“Among the assets prepared are around 2,450 boats and more than 3,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles and lorries, in addition to various other supporting assets.
“We have also prepared 170,000 ready-to-eat meals as initial food supplies for victims upon their arrival at relief centres, as well as 60,000 food kits containing essential items to be distributed to victims when they return to their homes,” he said.
He was speaking after appearing on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme, titled ‘Government Preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon’, here today.
Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.
Meanwhile, the Incident Command Centre is headed by a Disaster Operations Commander, who is the district police chief, with the district Fire and Rescue Station chief serving as the deputy. The Malaysian Civil Defence Force will assist in coordinating rescue and evacuation operations.
“Apart from rescue agencies, Nadma also mobilises community leaders, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and local communities through the Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) programme to support rescue operations and the management of relief centres,” he said.
At the same time, Abdul Gapar encouraged members of the public to download the Malaysia Disaster Information Management System (MyDIMS) application, launched by Nadma on April 24, to obtain disaster-related information.
He said the application sends notifications when users are within a 10-kilometre radius of a disaster-affected area. It also consolidates weather information, disaster updates and the locations of relief centres, including navigation guidance to these centres.
In addition, residents living in high-risk areas were reminded to keep emergency bags ready, containing important documents such as identity cards and passports, basic medication, food and drinking water supplies, as well as suitable clothing, in preparation for possible flooding. — Bernama

Title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
Article:
JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief.
“I have received sad news from Melaka. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.
“As Alor Gajah Keadilan deputy division chief, Brother Samivel had long served and remained loyal to the struggle. May his service and spirit continue to guide our steps as we carry on this struggle.
“My thoughts and prayers, and Azizah’s, are with the late Samivel’s family and fellow comrades. May they be given strength and fortitude in facing this trying ordeal,” Anwar said, speaking also for his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
The crash happened along Jalan Pondok Batang here at about noon, in front of PH’s main operations room for the Asahan seat, according to the New Straits Times.
Jasin district police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said police received information about the accident at about 12.45pm.
He said initial information showed that the car Samivel was in had collided with a lorry, which RTM reported was carrying fruit.
Lee said investigations were underway to determine the cause of the crash, and that more details would be released once police had the full picture.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said the department received an emergency call at 12.22pm.
He said rescuers found Samivel trapped in the driver’s seat, and that he was pronounced dead by Health Ministry personnel before being handed over to police.
Samivel’s body was taken to the forensic unit of Jasin Hospital for a post-mortem, the NST reported.
The PH Election Department described his death as a great loss to his family, friends, party members and everyone who knew him, the NST reported.
It also thanked him for his service and contributions, particularly his hard work throughout the state election campaign.
Sinar Harian reported that Samivel was among the “backbones” of the campaign of PH’s Asahan candidate P. Denesh.
Denesh, who was on a walkabout and house visits in Kampung Jus Permai at the time, rushed to the scene, when he heard the news.
Denesh is the challenger against Asahan incumbent from Barisan Nasional, Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam Roslan.

Title: Re-ignite the Malaysian Dream, Lim Kit Siang urges Melaka voters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Veteran DAP leader Lim Kit Siang today called on voters in Melaka to “re-ignite the Malaysian Dream”, describing Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation as a starting point for renewed efforts to build a united and world-class Malaysia.
In an open letter to the people of Melaka, Lim said Malaysians should embrace an identity that places nationality above ethnicity, where every citizen regards themselves as Malaysian first before identifying as Malay, Chinese, Indian, Kadazan, Iban or Orang Asli.
He said such a vision would help build a nation that is democratic, prosperous, committed to the rule of law and respectful of human rights.
Lim traced the roots of the “Malaysian Dream” to before independence, citing Chinese educationist Lim Lian Geok's 1956 message to Utusan Melayu on the need to cultivate a Malaysian mindset.
Recalling his political career, Lim said he was fielded by DAP to contest the Bandar Melaka parliamentary seat in 1969, describing the election as a battle for the Malaysian Dream.
He said he had not expected the Alliance coalition, which later became Barisan Nasional, to be defeated during his lifetime, but noted that this eventually happened in 2018, although the change in government lasted only until 2020.
According to Lim, meaningful reforms require sustained political commitment over one or two full terms in office, particularly with leaders from the country's largest community taking the lead in driving change.
While acknowledging that some reforms had been implemented, he said they did not go far enough, resulting in growing public disappointment.
Nevertheless, Lim urged Malaysians not to abandon the aspirations of the Malaysian Dream.
“I call on the voters of Malacca to represent the Malaysian nation to re-ignite the Malaysian Dream project to make Malaysia a great world-class nation by voting for every DAP and Pakatan Harapan candidate,” he said in the statement.

Title: Flood situation worsens in Selangor as evacuees increase, improves in Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The number of flood evacuees taking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Selangor continued to rise, while Perak recorded a decrease, as of 4 pm today.
In Selangor, the number of flood evacuees at five PPS in Kuala Selangor increased to 1,032 people, from 289 families, compared with 945 people from 265 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed the highest number of evacuees, at 416, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (287), SK Parit Mahang (238), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77) and SK Jaya Setia (12).
In Perak, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district decreased to 330 people, from 94 families, compared with 380 people, from 108 families, this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said that Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) housed 257 evacuees, while Dewan MPTI Langkap accommodated 73.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast rain and thunderstorms in all districts in Perak this afternoon and evening. — Bernama

Title: Funding Malaysia’s SMEs is about quality and not quantity, says economy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government wants to improve the quality of financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to strengthen local firms’ global competitiveness and enable workers to earn higher wages and hold better-quality jobs.
Although Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today that structural challenges still needed to be addressed so that SMEs could expand and improve productivity.
He said the main challenge was no longer simply ensuring firms had access to credit, but making sure the financing met their investment and expansion needs.
“The real issue is the quality of funding being channelled. It is not just about how firms obtain credit, but how we ensure our firms remain competitive globally.
“Particularly in ensuring productivity improvements that can eventually translate into higher wages and quality employment,” he told reporters after the launch of the World Bank’s 33rd Malaysia Economic Monitor, titled ‘From Quantity to Quality: Financing Malaysia’s Productive SMEs’, here today.
Akmal said the government had taken note of the World Bank’s recommendations, including broadening the range of assets that could be accepted as collateral.
He said relying on conventional collateral such as property could limit firms’ access to loans, even when they had other assets that could serve as security.
“Among the problems in obtaining loans is the collateral requirement, which typically requires property to be pledged as security.
“Yet firms also have other assets that should be considered, such as machinery and accounts receivable, to broaden the financing options available to them,” he said.
He added that financing mechanisms also needed to be implemented more transparently so that firms received facilities suited to their needs.
The report found that about 38 per cent of firms in Malaysia had loans or credit facilities, while loan approval rates rose from about 68 per cent in 2015 to 86 per cent in 2024.
However, it also found that SMEs still financed about two-thirds of their fixed-asset investments with internal funds, while external financing relied heavily on bank debt, with limited access to equity and other forms of risk capital.
The World Bank also highlighted that financing constraints could undermine firms’ ability to invest in innovation, improve productivity and expand.
Akmal said the push to improve financing quality was in line with the government’s aspirations under the 13th Malaysia Plan, particularly in raising productivity and strengthening economic competitiveness.
He said Malaysia’s economy remained resilient, having expanded 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, with the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s advance estimate showing 5.3 per cent growth in the third quarter.
The World Bank had also raised its 2026 growth forecast for Malaysia to 5.1 per cent, up 0.7 percentage point from its previous projection.
The Malaysia Economic Monitor is the World Bank’s regular assessment of Malaysia’s economic developments and outlook, and its 33rd edition focuses on how financing instruments can help SMEs overcome investment constraints, improve productivity and grow.

Title: Kelantan exco shake-up: Deputy MB says Bersatu rep’s appointment not renewed, with Sultan’s consent
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — Ayer Lanas assemblyman Datuk Kamarudin Md Nor’s appointment as a Kelantan state executive council (exco) member was not renewed, effective November 9.
Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the decision had received the consent of the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V.
He said the two portfolios previously held by Kamarudin would be redistributed to two existing exco members to ensure the smooth running of state administration.
“The Tourism and Arts portfolio will be overseen by exco member Hilmi Abdullah, while the Heritage and Culture portfolio will be taken over by Zamakhsyari Mohamad. The decision takes immediate effect,” he said in a statement today.
The state government also expressed its appreciation and gratitude to Kamarudin for his service and contributions during his tenure as a member of the Kelantan exco.
It also acknowledged his commitment and dedication in discharging the responsibilities entrusted to him throughout his term.
Yesterday, media reports quoted Kamarudin as confirming that he had received a letter terminating his exco appointment.
However, he declined to disclose the contents of the letter at the time.
Kamarudin previously oversaw the Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage portfolio.
Meanwhile, at a press conference, Kamarudin said he accepted the state government’s decision not to renew his appointment as an Exco member.
He said that although he was no longer part of the Exco line-up, his relationship with the state government and its leadership remained cordial in his capacity as an assemblyman.
Asked why he had not resigned after PAS announced its decision to sever ties with Bersatu last June, Kamarudin said, “It was because I was waiting for Sultan Muhammad V’s consent on the revocation of my Exco appointment. I hope all parties understand this.”
He also dismissed claims that his performance while overseeing the Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage portfolio had been unsatisfactory, describing such allegations as inaccurate.
He said that during his more than two years in charge of the portfolio, his initial focus was on promoting Kelantan as a tourist destination, before placing greater emphasis on cultural development in his final year.
Among the achievements he highlighted were the launch of direct flights between Kota Bharu and Jakarta, which recorded a 71 per cent passenger load factor, and the arrival of 12.5 million domestic tourists in Kelantan last year.
“I would like to express my appreciation to Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud for the trust and opportunity given to me to serve as a state Exco member for three years,” said the state Bersatu chairman. — Bernama

Title: Skudai Deepavali fireworks stunt ends in court for four, one just 16
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 11 — Four men, including a secondary school student, claimed trial at the Magistrate’s Court here today to charges of setting off fireworks on a main road during Deepavali last Sunday.
The accused – P. Ruban, 20; S. Tharun, 18; H. Periuthiv, 19; and a 16-year-old – entered their pleas after the charges were read to them separately.
Their pleas were recorded before four different magistrates: A. Shaarmini, Atifah Hazimah Wahab, Nurzihan Abdul Rehman and Nur Fatin Mohamad Farid.
According to the charge sheets, all of the accused allegedly acted negligently with fireworks, an explosive substance, on a public road occupied by other vehicles, in a manner that could have caused harm to others.
The incident allegedly took place at 1.30am last Sunday on Jalan Skudai-Gelang Patah, near the Taman Nesa traffic lights junction in Skudai.
Ruban, Tharun and Periuthiv were charged under Section 286 of the Penal Code for negligent conduct with respect to an explosive substance, which carries a maximum sentence of six months’ imprisonment, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both upon conviction.
The 16-year-old who cannot be identified under the Child Act was charged under the same section and, if convicted, could be subject to various court orders, including being discharged with a warning, entering into a good-behaviour bond with conditions set by the court, paying a fine, performing community service, or being sent to an approved school or the Henry Gurney School.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Eizlan Azhar, Adilah Farzana Che Ad, Izdhiyah Zahirah Ahmad Ghazali and Nor Hidayah Mohd Tarmizi proposed bail of RM3,000 and RM10,000 respectively.
However, lawyer T. Monisha Dhaarcayinii, who represented all the accused, asked for the bail amounts to be reduced.
She said her clients did not pose a flight risk.
The court set bail at between RM1,500 and RM3,000 for each of the accused and fixed December 3 for mention and submission of documents.
Separately, two other men – M. Rubenkumar, 23, and Muhammad Irsyad, 19 – claimed trial to charges of riding motorcycles in a manner likely to cause danger or unreasonable obstruction to traffic.
The charges were read to them separately before Nur Fatin.
Each was accused of riding a motorcycle in circles, at the same location and time as the fireworks incident.
They were charged under Section 48(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for obstructing vehicles, which carries a maximum penalty of one year’s imprisonment, a fine of up to RM5,000, or both upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Traffic Prosecuting Officer Inspector Mohd Khairul Azhar Pakrudin, while both accused were represented by Monisha.
Each was granted bail of RM2,500 with one surety, and the case was fixed for mention on December 11.
Last Sunday, it was reported that police were searching for a group of men suspected of setting off fireworks on a main road in Skudai.
Four men were arrested later that day.
Three more men were arrested yesterday in connection with the incident.
Of the seven men arrested, six were later charged in court, while the other was released on bail and will serve as a prosecution witness.

Title: Anwar: ‘Hundreds of years of service’ no excuse, corrupt people belong in prison
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said that even hundreds of years of service cannot justify letting anyone plunder the wealth of the people and the country.
He added that those who commit corruption belong in prison.
“Even hundreds of years of service cannot be a reason for us to let anyone plunder and rob the wealth of the people and the country. This attitude of compromising with corruption in the name of service is far from the teachings of Islam.
“This ‘tolerance for evil’ is what is ruining us. Those of us who hate and oppose corruption must speak louder and send a clear message that those who commit corruption belong in prison,” he said in a Facebook post.
He did not name anyone, but the post comes a day after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was transferred from Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his six-year SRC International jail sentence under house arrest in Jalan Langgak Duta.
The transfer follows a conditional royal pardon that allows him to serve it at home until August 23, 2028.
He was originally sentenced to 12 years’ jail and fined RM210 million in July 2020 over RM42 million in SRC International funds, before the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved the term and cut the fine to RM50 million in January 2024.
Umno paid the RM50 million fine last Friday, after which the High Court issued an order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

Title: What are the terms of Najib’s house arrest? Saifuddin Nasution to explain in Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he will address the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow to lay out the operational conditions and custodial restrictions governing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s transition into house arrest.
Saifuddin Nasution told the
New Straits Times
that he would provide a full explanation to lawmakers following mounting public scrutiny regarding how the unprecedented home detention arrangement will be enforced on the ground.
“I’ll answer all those questions in Parliament tomorrow,” he said.
The minister was responding to press queries over the specific parameters of Najib’s confinement, including whether his immediate family can reside with him at his private residence, what visitor protocols will apply, and how correctional authorities plan to monitor his movements.
The upcoming parliamentary briefing follows Najib’s arrival at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence in Kuala Lumpur at 9.27pm yesterday to begin serving the remainder of his six-year SRC International sentence at home.
The 73-year-old former prime minister was transported from Kajang Prison in a silver Proton X70, escorted by a heavily guarded convoy of Prisons Department and police patrol vehicles.
His release from prison walls was finalised after High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin set aside a contentious November 6 discharge order and replaced it in full, explicitly authorizing Najib to serve his custodial sentence at his private home until August 23, 2028.
The judge directed the court registrar to issue a perfected warrant of release following arguments presented by defence counsel and deputy public prosecutors.
The High Court intervened after the Attorney General’s Chambers sought a formal review to eliminate legal ambiguities in the earlier order’s wording and enforceability, a process that briefly kept Najib incarcerated in Kajang Prison while the procedural technicalities were resolved.
The house detention regime stems from a conditional royal pardon granted on September 18 by the Federal Territories Pardons Board, which was formally triggered after Najib settled the required RM50 million fine.
Najib was convicted in 2020 for the misappropriation of RM42 million in SRC International funds and sentenced to 12 years in prison and a RM210 million fine, penalties that were subsequently halved by the Pardons Board in January 2024.

Title: Monsoon surge triggers continuous rain alert for Kelantan, Terengganu and Sabah until tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 – The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) has issued an updated continuous rain alert for parts of Kelantan, Terengganu, and Sabah, as an incoming monsoon surge threatens to trigger persistent downpours through tomorrow.
In an advisory released at 2.00pm today, the department explained that atmospheric simulation models indicate a monsoon surge is entering regional airspace, creating unstable weather conditions likely to dump sustained, heavy precipitation along the eastern seaboard of Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Sabah over the next 24 hours.
In the peninsula, the alert covers seven districts in Kelantan: Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Machang, and Tanah Merah. In neighbouring Terengganu, the warning encompasses the northern and coastal districts of Besut, Setiu, Kuala Terengganu, and Kuala Nerus.
Across East Malaysia, the advisory targets northern and eastern Sabah, specifically covering Kudat and Pitas within the Kudat division, alongside Paitan in the Sandakan division.
The “Alert” designation serves as the initial tier on the department’s three-stage continuous rain alert scale, warning that sustained rainfall is projected to affect the identified localities.
MET Malaysia urged residents, particularly those in low-lying and flood-prone settlements, to track real-time weather movements through the myCuaca mobile application, the department's official web portal, and verified social media channels, or call its 24-hour hotline at 1-300-22-1638 for inquiries.

Title: Loke: JPJ’s war on overloaded lorries must continue even without me, as it involves human lives
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — In his parting words to the Transport Ministry, Anthony Loke today urged the Road Transport Department to continue its “war” against overloading in commercial vehicles even after he leaves as transport minister.
Loke, who effectively resigned as transport minister yesterday, said there would be people cheering that the minister who refused to compromise on overloading, and who they felt interfered with their livelihood, was gone.
“‘The minister has left, we can overload again like in the past, no problem,’” he said in his 48-minute speech at the Transport Ministry here, describing how overloaders would feel.
“I want JPJ to prove them wrong. This war on overloading will be continued, with or without me,” he said, using the Malay abbreviation for Road Transport Department by which it is better known locally.
“This is not an issue of minister, this is an issue of human lives. This is not an issue of livelihood, this is an issue of human lives,” he said.
He said whoever succeeds him as minister, and whoever becomes JPJ director-general, must carry on the mission without delay or softening, because it is vital for road safety.
He urged JPJ enforcement officers to act against overloading, illegal racing and speeding, which he said cause road accidents and deaths, noting that the law had been amended to give JPJ enforcement powers over such offences.
Looking back at his tenure as transport minister from December 2022 to yesterday, Loke said two fatal road accidents within a few weeks had left a huge psychological impact on him.
“I feel very guilty, why we cannot avoid such an incident,” he said.
He said so many innocent lives, including youths and students, were lost that he asked whether something could not have been done to prevent such a tragedy, after which the ministry pursued multiple new road safety policies, initiatives and measures.
The accidents he referred to were the May 13, 2025 collision in Teluk Intan between an overloaded lorry and a Federal Reserve Unit truck that killed nine personnel, and the June 9, 2025 crash of a chartered bus along the Gerik-Jeli East-West Highway that killed 15 Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris students.
He urged whoever holds the post to make road safety the ministry’s main agenda in policy, measures and law, saying it would be unforgivable not to pursue it wholeheartedly.
Anthony Loke urged his successor at the Transport Ministry to make policies on road safety that focuses on curbing fatalities. — File picture by Farhan Najib
Earlier today at the ministry’s monthly assembly, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the ministry’s declared war on overloaded commercial vehicles meant a lot to him, and that he had told Loke so personally.
“I worked at the Public Works Department previously for 22 years, many of my roads were damaged because of overloading,” he said.
He said millions of ringgit had been spent repairing the damaged roads, and that overloading had also caused accidents.
Hasbi said that as a government officer he had previously fought overloading as a mere battle, and was glad when Loke declared it a war, which he said meant a lot for the people.
Continue FLYsiswa subsidies for students’ flights forever, Loke urges
Among other things, Loke highlighted achievements during his tenure, including the digitalisation of JPJ’s services and the JPJeBid system for bidding on vehicle number plates.
He credited JPJ’s internal JPJeBid team with devising the online bidding system since 2018, during his first stint as transport minister, saying it had become both a good source of government revenue and a way of increasing transparency for users.
Loke also pointed to the FLYsiswa flight ticket subsidy for university students travelling between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak, which he said the ministry “created out of nothing” because it had never existed in the government budget.
He said the ministry started it without any allocation or injection from the Finance Ministry, funding it boldly with proceeds from the sale of special vehicle number plates.
He said the Finance Ministry recognised the initiative in subsequent years, and it is now a line item in the annual Budget, which makes it permanent for as long as the ministry continues the policy.
Noting that the ministry started with a RM300 subsidy that has since risen to RM400, Loke said the amount may seem small but is meaningful help for families who could not afford flights to send their children to university.
“I always stress, what we do in the Transport Ministry, we must remember we are Transport Ministry for Malaysia, not just Transport Ministry for the peninsula,” he said.
Loke said policies must be inclusive of Malaysians in Sabah and Sarawak, which was the spirit behind FLYsiswa, adding that he hoped it would continue “forever” in what was his final speech at a Transport Ministry monthly assembly.

Title: Umno says opposing Najib’s house arrest could amount to challenging King’s constitutional powers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Umno has warned that actions perceived as protests against the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, including the house arrest provision, could be construed as challenging the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional authority.
In a media statement posted on his Facebook page, Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party believed the conditional pardon granted under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution reflected the King’s constitutional powers and rights, which must be respected by all institutions and the public.
Umno also expressed its gratitude to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for what it described as His Majesty’s firm decree concerning the conditional pardon that led to the implementation of house arrest for Najib.
The party said any action taken in protest, including using the conditional pardon decree as justification, could be seen as an act of defiance against the King’s constitutional authority.
Umno reiterated that it would remain steadfast in defending the dignity and sovereignty of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay Rulers.
It also stressed that Malaysia was a nation governed by law and that all legal processes must remain within the framework of the Federal Constitution.
The party said it was the responsibility of all Malaysians to uphold and defend that constitutional framework.
The statement ended with the words: “Daulat Tuanku.”

Title: Rosmah not allowed to live with Najib during house arrest, Umno leader says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s family members and other individuals are not permitted to live with him while he serves the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, according to Umno Women’s executive council member Datuk Nurulhidayah Ahmad Zahid.
Nurulhidayah said Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, is expected to stay at her residence in Pavilion instead of the Taman Duta house where he is serving his sentence,
Harian Metro reported today.
Responding to questions on Threads about the implementation of the house arrest order, Nurulhidayah said the Jalan Langgak Duta residence had been gazetted as a prison, meaning standard prison rules would apply.
She also claimed that online food purchases would not be allowed and that all meals and drinks would be determined by prison authorities.
She added that visiting hours would be set by the authorities and carried out according to procedures similar to those in prisons.
Yesterday, High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin set aside a release order issued on November 6 and replaced it with an order transferring Najib from Kajang Prison to his residence with immediate effect, in line with a conditional pardon order.
The order allows Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence under house detention until August 23, 2028, following his conviction in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case.

Title: ‘Camera must follow the schedule’: Hannah Yeoh says as DBKL makes body cams compulsory for field operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will equip its enforcement unit with 200 additional body-worn cameras, bringing its total number of devices to 305.
Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud announced the expansion at DBKL’s 57th Enforcement Day parade in Bandar Tun Razak today.
“I have directed the enforcement unit to ensure that for every operation, the schedule must follow the camera, not the camera following the schedule.
“This means whenever they go out to enforce the law, wearing them is mandatory,” Yeoh said.
She said the initiative was intended to protect enforcement officers from baseless allegations while ensuring they maintained integrity and followed the law during field operations.
She said the system would initially operate on a pilot basis, modelled after the police force’s experience, with footage retained for six months under the management of DBKL’s integrity unit.
She added that the system would be reviewed and improved over time, while members of the public could lodge complaints or request internal reviews of footage.
Fadlun said the additional cameras were part of DBKL’s efforts to modernise enforcement operations, with footage providing a record of officers’ actions in the event of complaints or disputes.
DBKL first tested body-worn cameras through a five-device pilot in 2020 before making their use mandatory in 2024, and is now updating its guidelines on device usage, evidence handling and public complaints.
Separately, Yeoh welcomed DBKL’s introduction of more weather-appropriate T-shirts for its Patrol Unit, saying officers’ comfort and safety should remain priorities during field duties.

Title: BN MPs want AG to take leave over four-day delay in Najib’s house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Several Barisan Nasional (BN) MPs today called for the Attorney General (AG) to be placed on temporary leave pending an independent investigation into the delay in implementing Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest.
The lawmakers said yesterday’s fresh High Court order had upheld justice but did not absolve the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) of responsibility for what they described as serious administrative oversights that had damaged public confidence in the institution.
“The implementation of house arrest does not erase the delay, and a settlement does not eliminate accountability; the AG must answer why the deferral occurred and who is responsible,” Tenggara MP Manndzri Nasib said, reading aloud from a statement in a press conference at Parliament here.
“The King’s decree must be upheld, court orders must be complied with, and justice must never be used as a tool for political games,” he added.
The BN MPs questioned the AGC’s handling of Najib’s detention after he paid the RM50 million fine imposed in his SRC International case on November 6, arguing that the payment should have triggered his immediate transfer to house arrest.
Manndzri said Najib’s continued detention at Kajang Prison for four more days could amount to unlawful detention, particularly as no court order had been obtained to justify the delay.
The statement also questioned the AG’s role as a member of the Pardons Board during its September 18 meeting, asking if practical arrangements and legal implications of implementing Najib’s house arrest had been discussed then.
Manndzri said that if potential legal or administrative issues had been identified during that meeting, the necessary steps should have been taken before the fine was paid to prevent delays.
Najib was transferred from Kajang Prison to his residence last night to serve the remainder of his six-year SRC International prison sentence under house arrest, following a fresh High Court order.
The new order was issued after the AGC sought a review of the November 6 discharge order, citing concerns that it contained defects and required clarification to ensure it was consistent with the conditional pardon granted by the King.
Najib’s lawyers had maintained that the original order was valid in substance despite grammatical errors, arguing that its instruction for him to be released from Kajang Prison to serve his remaining sentence under house arrest was clear.

Title: DAP yet to pick candidate to replace Loke as transport minister, for PM to decide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today confirmed that DAP has yet to discuss a candidate to replace him as transport minister, a post he resigned from with immediate effect yesterday.
Asked by reporters at the Transport Ministry here whether DAP had discussed a potential successor, Loke gave a brief “not yet” response.
“This is the prime minister's jurisdiction, discuss with him,” he replied when asked whether or not the decision would be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Asked if he would reconsider his resignation as Anwar did not want him to leave the post, Loke reiterated that his decision is unchanged.
“As far as I'm concerned, my resignation's already effective yesterday. I will stop my duties beginning today,” he said.
Asked whether he planned to return to the post after the next general election, Loke said he would address the matter after the election.
On his priorities ahead of the next general election, Loke said: “Of course my focus is that I'm the party secretary-general, I have to focus on my party building, my role as MP and to continue to support the PM as PH.”
PH stands for Pakatan Harapan, the ruling coalition which includes DAP.
Loke was also asked whether two proposed constitutional reforms – separating the roles of the attorney general and public prosecutor, and limiting the prime minister's tenure – would be passed by Parliament during its current term.
“That one definitely we hope will be brought to Parliament this term before the dissolution of Parliament. So as far as I'm concerned, that's the collective decision of the Cabinet.
“And for DAP of course we stood by it. We want these two constitutional amendments to be tabled, and we will definitely support these amendments,” he said.
Loke's resignation took effect on November 10 following the High Court's decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.

Title: Ex-Tabung Haji chief Azeez gets court nod to challenge IRB’s cancellation of RM4.8m tax deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim today secured High Court permission to challenge the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) decision to revoke a RM4.8 million tax settlement he says he had fully paid.
The court today allowed his application for leave to commence judicial review, paving the way for a full hearing on whether IRB was legally entitled to cancel the agreement.
Azeez’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said the court was satisfied that there were legal issues that warranted further examination, local media reported this afternoon.
“After hearing submissions from both parties, the court is satisfied that there are legal issues to be heard in our leave application,” he told reporters after the hearing, according to news portal
Free Malaysia Today.
The dispute centres on a settlement agreement signed on February 9, 2022, covering Azeez’s tax and penalties for the assessment years 2011 to 2020.
The agreement fixed his total liability at RM4.8 million, which was to be paid through 25 monthly instalments.
Azeez maintained that he had paid the full amount, but IRB informed him in a letter dated August 7 that it had revoked the agreement and the subsequent composite assessment after discovering new facts and income that had not previously been taken into account.
According to
The Edge
, Azeez is now seeking to have the revocation and the composite assessment notice dated March 22, 2022, quashed, as well as a court order compelling IRB to honour the original agreement.
His legal challenge argues that the settlement and composite assessment were final and conclusive under the Income Tax Act 1967.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers opposed his application, arguing that it was premature as investigations were still ongoing and IRB had not imposed any fresh tax liability on him.
The court also granted a two-week interim stay to prevent IRB from taking further action against Azeez while the judicial review proceedings are pending.
Case management is scheduled on November 16 to fix hearing dates for the judicial review and the stay application.

Title: Trader suspected of sourcing frozen chicken from Thailand arrested in raid
Article:
-KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — A frozen chicken trader in Pasir Tumboh, here, is suspected of obtaining between 300 and 500 boxes of stock from a supplier in Thailand before selling them at his wholesale premises.
General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the matter came to light following the arrest of a 38-year-old man during an Op Salju Mega raid at a premises along Jalan Pasir Puteh, Kampung Pasir Tumboh, at about noon yesterday.
He said the suspect claimed that the frozen chicken had been brought into the country legally through the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) complex before being sold at his wholesale outlet.
“An inspection by the enforcement team uncovered 209 boxes of frozen chicken, weighing 2,508 kilogrammes and worth RM42,845, stored in a refrigerated container at the premises,” he said in a statement last night.
He added that the raid was conducted by the Intelligence Branch of the GOF 8th Battalion in collaboration with the Kota Bharu Municipal Council - Islamic City (MPKB-BRI).
According to him, the inspection also found that the trader had failed to produce valid business documents, proof of ownership or authorisation to store the frozen chicken.
Following this, MPKB-BRI issued an offence notice and a compound notice against the man for operating a business without a valid licence and improperly disposing of waste in a public area.
Ahmad Radzi said the suspect and the seized items had been handed over to MPKB-BRI for further action, while the relevant documentation had been forwarded to the Kelantan branch of the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
He said unlicensed business activities not only hampered monitoring by the authorities but could also result in revenue losses for the state government through unpaid licence fees and other related charges.
“This situation can also create unfair competition for business operators who comply with regulations, while undermining the effectiveness of enforcement by local authorities,” he said.
He added that continuous monitoring would be carried out to ensure business activities complied with licensing requirements and did not compromise cleanliness, public health or community well-being. — Bernama

Title: Social media firms face Dec 28 deadline under Online Safety Act
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Licensed social media service providers must submit their Online Safety Plans to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) by Dec 28 at the latest, in compliance with the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866).
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the plans must detail the measures and improvements that platform providers intend to implement to ensure a safer digital environment for users.
She said social media platforms were also expected to implement user age verification requirements in early January 2027, following the end of the current transition period.
“We are still in the transition period, and we expect platforms to implement this obligation in early January next year. All data on the number of accounts they have verified and closed will be submitted to us after the transition period,” she said during Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The deputy minister said this in reply to Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang), who sought clarification on social media platforms’ compliance with age verification requirements, including the number of accounts verified and blocked, as well as action against service providers that failed to meet their obligations.
Teo said MCMC had issued directives to social media service providers, including Meta, TikTok and Google, to ensure the implementation of age verification mechanisms. The commission had also requested relevant information to monitor and assess compliance.
She said licensed service providers that failed to fulfil their obligations under the Online Safety Act could face enforcement action, including fines of up to RM1 million and an additional fine of up to RM100,000 for each day the offence continued after conviction.
On the threats posed by fake accounts and hate speech, Teo clarified that the age verification mechanism for social media users aged 16 and above did not involve verifying their identities.
As such, she said, the mechanism would not directly address the problem of fake accounts, which required further examination and discussion on appropriate measures. — Bernama

Title: MCMC finds 23 internet quality breaches in Muar, takes action against telcos
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has issued eight non-compliance notices to telecommunications companies after an audit this year uncovered 23 breaches of internet service quality standards at 16 locations in the Muar parliamentary constituency.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the audit, conducted on six service providers between Jan 1 and Oct 1, found that only 18 of the 34 locations assessed in Muar met the Mandatory Standards for Quality of Service (MSQoS).
“Of the 23 cases of non-compliance identified, 18 have been resolved through network improvements, while MCMC is taking follow-up action on the remaining five, including requiring service providers to submit plans to improve their services.
“Failure to comply with these directives may result in enforcement action under existing laws,” she said when replying to a question from Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Syed Saddiq had wanted to know the measures to address poor internet service quality and limited connectivity in parts of Muar, despite data from the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) showing 100 per cent coverage in Parit Amat, Sungai Kelat, Tanjung Tohor and Sungai Muda.
Teo said internet coverage in populated areas of the Muar parliamentary constituency had reached 99.98 per cent under JENDELA, but high coverage rates did not necessarily mean users would experience the same quality of service everywhere.
She said internet service quality could also be affected by network congestion, disruptions to telecommunications infrastructure, and local geographical and environmental conditions.
To address connectivity issues, she said CelcomDigi and U Mobile had completed two Portable Base Transceiver Station (PBTS) towers in Tanjung Tohor and Sungai Terap following complaints from the Muar parliamentary office in November 2025.
Meanwhile, Teo said Maxis is building a new telecommunications tower in Sri Menanti, which is expected to be completed next month, while network improvements in Parit Amat were carried out in December 2025.
“Three more telecommunications towers are also being built under the JENDELA initiative in Kampung Sungai Muda, Kampung Sungai Balang Kechil Darat and Kampung Sungai Balang Darat.
“Construction is under way, and the towers are expected to be completed and operational by December 2026,” she said. — Her

Title: ‘A leader must be decisive’: Loke says ‘conscience is clear’ as he reflects on time as minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today said his conscience is clear as he had done his best during his nearly four years as transport minister, while reaffirming that his resignation took effect yesterday following the court order allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest.
Speaking at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and Deepavali celebrations today, Loke thanked everyone in the ministry and apologised to anyone who may have been affected by his words, actions or past mistakes.
“But my conscience is clear that I tried my best to carry out my duties and responsibilities,” he said in his 48-minute speech at the ministry here.
Loke said it was not that he was firm or bold in making decisions, as others described him, but that he believed a key leadership value was “to be decisive”.
Reflecting on his two stints as transport minister, from 2018 to 2020 and from December 2022 to November 2026, he said decisiveness was one of the key lessons he had learnt.
“Not up to six years, but during the time when I held this position as minister, one thing I learnt is that a leader must be decisive,” he said.
Loke said civil servants were “most worried and disliked it the most when a minister sits on a decision, sits on files, not making decisions”.
“Although sometimes the decisions are not perfect, not 100 per cent correct, there will be side-effects, but we learn. When there is a decision, if it is not correct, we correct it.
“But most importantly, a leader must be decisive. That is what I tried to do, to be a decisive minister,” he said.
He added that mistakes should be lessons that make the ministry better and more excellent.
“I hope my contribution in the few years of leading this ministry will leave a positive impact for the future of our country and society,” he said, before ending his speech by wishing those celebrating a Happy Deepavali and thanking everyone for their cooperation.
Loke’s speech was greeted with a standing ovation from ministry officials attending the monthly assembly.
Earlier in his speech, Loke left no room for doubt that his resignation yesterday was his own decision, one he intended to see through.
Noting that politicians are often ranked among the least trusted because they do not do as they say, he said he chose to be one who does, to loud applause from the audience.
“To me, positions can be lost, but credibility must be retained,” he said, drawing applause again.
Loke said this was a principle taught by his father: that one must fulfil what one says, even when it is bitter or difficult.
He also noted the ministry’s mix of races and religions, saying he had led it with Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan as a team that worked together regardless of race.
Loke said he and Hasbi, who belong to different political parties, had never had a problem working together.
“I never considered him as deputy or Number Two, but as a team that takes responsibility together,” he said.
He said people had expected their different parties to cause friction, but in four years there was none.
Loke thanked Hasbi for his cooperation, adding that he respected him as a senior and welcomed his views.
Anthony Loke (centre) with Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah (left) and Transport Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan (right) at the Transport Ministry in Putrajaya on November 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Hasbi, in his speech earlier, said it was an “honour” to have worked with Loke and that, despite their different backgrounds, they shared the same goal of serving the nation.
He described Loke as a minister who went on the ground to listen to the public and put public interest first, and said the policies, systems and culture of work excellence Loke instilled would continue.
Revealing that he had heard the prime minister had yet to receive Loke’s resignation letter, Hasbi said he had urged Loke to reconsider.
“YB, come on
lah
, I hope you change your mind
lah
,” he said, adding that he had told Loke there was still much work to be done.
But even with that, Loke made it clear that he had resigned.
Jana Santhiran, in a 22-minute speech, presented a “report card” of the ministry’s achievements under Loke over the past four years, citing 55 initiatives across four sectors and five focus areas.
He praised Loke’s principled leadership and courage in making decisions, saying these had given the ministry clear direction while putting the public first.
Saying Loke’s legacy would be far more meaningful than the numbers in the report card,Jana Santhiran thanked the former on behalf of the ministry.
